content:
inc-bot: ALERT: spike in 5xx (502/504) from private-vpc peering path -> inference-gateway-prod (eu-west1). error-rate ~18% over 5m. paging eng-sre and netops.

Mia L: saw the alert, on it. which customer pool first?

Alex R: looks like majority of errors from customer_pools: ['fintech-alpha', 'retail-beta'] hitting routed peering -> transit-appliance-02. lots of TLS handshake timeouts in app logs.

Mia L: posting quick graphs: requests/s stable, but TLS handshake failures up and upstream 502s.

Mia L: metrics snapshot: total reqs 4.2k/min, 5xx 760/min (~18%). p50 latency +10ms, p95 spikes at 2s.

Mia L: tcpdump on transit-appliance-02 shows SYNs retransmitted, then client RSTs.

Mia L: ```
14:07:12.432 SYN a.b.c.d.443 > 10.4.5.6.43212: S seq 0
14:07:12.732 SYN a.b.c.d.443 > 10.4.5.6.43212: S seq 0 (retrans)
14:07:13.032 RST 10.4.5.6.43212 > a.b.c.d.443
```

Alex R: flow logs show asymmetric src/dst NAT for same conn — replies coming back via different egress IP. suspect SNAT drift / conntrack mismatch on transit appliances after peering maintenance at 14:00.

NetOps Bot: note: peering route update propagated at 14:01 UTC from cloud provider (change-id: r-20260314-137).

Jordan (SRE): can someone dump conntrack on the transit node? I want to see entries for the affected client IPs.

Mia L: running conntrack -L | grep 43212 -> shows two entries with different tuple translations (duplicate SNATs).

Mia L: ```
# conntrack -L | grep 43212
tcp      6 431999 ESTABLISHED src=10.4.5.6 dst=a.b.c.d sport=43212 dport=443 src=198.51.100.12 dst=203.0.113.5 sport=443 dport=43212 [ASSURED] use=1
tcp      6 431998 ESTABLISHED src=10.4.5.6 dst=a.b.c.d sport=43212 dport=443 src=198.51.100.13 dst=203.0.113.5 sport=443 dport=43212 [ASSURED] use=1
```

Alex R: that confirms SNAT collision/duplication. likely two NAT paths active and return path selected different egress IP -> backend sees invalid session -> TLS handshake timed out -> 502.

Jordan (SRE): mitigation plan: 1) temporarily pin SNAT to single egress IP on affected transit nodes, 2) flush conntrack for affected ranges, 3) roll back peering route change if needed.

Mia L: executing conntrack flush for the top affected client block now:

Mia L: ```
sudo conntrack -D -s 203.0.113.0/24
```

Mia L: applying iptables rule to force MASQUERADE on outbound interface (quick, reversible):

Mia L: ```
sudo iptables -t nat -A POSTROUTING -o eth1 -j MASQUERADE
# eth1 is egress to peering/transit
```

NetOps Bot: detected an overlapping route advertisement from partner at 14:02 that could cause return path via alternate egress.

Alex R: can we add temporary policy on routing layer to prefer egress-ip 198.51.100.12 for peering to the affected ASN? If so we avoid asymmetric return.

Mia L: requested route preference update to netops. @NetOps Bot can you push the policy?

NetOps Bot: queued policy change, will apply to transit group tg-02 in 45s.

Priya (PM): what is customer impact window? need to notify CS and possibly customers.

Sofia (Support): start draft: "We detected elevated 502/504 errors impacting inference requests for customers in EU. We're applying routing fixes and will update in 30m. If you're seeing errors, please DM support with request IDs." Thoughts?

Ken (Sales): flagging: fintech-alpha SLA is at-risk, their production jobs are timing out. Please keep me looped for customer comms.

Mia L: after conntrack flush + iptables MASQUERADE, 5xx dropped to ~6% within 3m.

Mia L: metric snippet: 5xx count: 760 -> 255 in 3m. p95 latency back to normal ~120ms.

Alex R: route pref applied by netops. I'm seeing consistent SNAT -> 198.51.100.12 on new flows. return path symmetric now.

Jordan (SRE): keep monitoring for 30m, we'll keep iptables rule for now and schedule a safe rollback with netops after longer observation. also will roll a small hotfix to ensure SNAT affinity on transit appliances.

Priya (PM): action items: 1) CX update in 15m (Sofia), 2) follow-up RCA doc (Jordan), 3) revert peering change with partner (NetOps), 4) consider permanent SNAT affinity config (Eng).

Sofia (Support): posting customer note to affected workspaces now: short transparent notice + call to open tickets.

Ken (Sales): thanks — reaching out to fintech-alpha lead to offer workaround (dedicated routing) while we verify stability.

Mia L: 30m check: error-rate steady at ~1.2%. holding mitigation. will hand off to night oncall in 45m.

Jordan (SRE): documented mitigation steps in incident tracker. leaving oncall in 45m, taking handoff summary now.

Jordan (SRE): ONCALL HANDOFF -> next: Jordan (SRE) 23:00-07:00. Summary: transient asymmetric peering after partner route update caused SNAT duplication on transit appliances leading to TLS handshake failures and 502/504. Mitigations applied: conntrack flush, temporary MASQUERADE iptables, route preference to egress-ip 198.51.100.12. Current status: stable, monitoring.

Mia L: adding runbook link and list of affected customer pools to tracker.

inc-bot: INCIDENT STATUS: mitigated -> monitoring. paging cleared for now.
